predictions.quote: I think that we are headed for it seems like a recession.
predictions.prediction: The U.S. economy will enter a recession in the near term following this April 2023 discussion, i.e., during the 2023 economic cycle.

predictions.quote: I think by the end of this year, 30% of knowledge work could be done by this.
predictions.prediction: By December 31, 2023, large language model–based AI systems (e.g., ChatGPT-4 and similar tools) will be capable of performing roughly 30% of the tasks currently done by typical white‑collar knowledge workers, at a quality level sufficient to be practically usable in real businesses.

predictions.quote: If you hear my voice right now and you're a white collar worker or knowledge worker and you're not using this this year and getting up to speed on it, I think you'll be out of a job within the next two GS.
predictions.prediction: Any white‑collar/knowledge worker who does not start using and getting up to speed on modern AI tools (like ChatGPT-4) during 2023 will lose their job and be unable to compete in the labor market within roughly the following two years (by around the end of 2025).

predictions.quote: I don't know, I think everything's going to cost about ten. All this knowledge work is going to be 10% as expensive to do. I don't think it's 10% less Chamath or you know, I think it's like 90% $0.10 on the dollar to knowledge work.
predictions.prediction: Within roughly the next 1–2.5 years from April 2023 ("five quarter ten" timeframe), the effective cost of performing white‑collar knowledge work, when leveraging AI tools, will fall by about 90%, to roughly 10% of its previous level.

predictions.quote: So you're going to be sitting on that property for five years, ten years before the market comes back the way that you need it to.
predictions.prediction: Owners who buy heavily vacant San Francisco office towers at distressed prices in 2023 will need to hold them for approximately 5–10 years before office demand and rents recover enough for the investment to make economic sense.

predictions.quote: So they're at 30% plus. And like I said, it could get worse before it gets better because as Lisa's role people are going to shed more space that they might not already be subleasing. So the real number might be like 40%.
predictions.prediction: San Francisco’s downtown office vacancy rate, which is already above 30% in April 2023, will likely rise further and may reach around 40% as existing leases roll off and tenants shed additional space over the subsequent few years.

predictions.quote: I mean, five years plus. I mean, just to give you some numbers... So they're at 30% plus. And like I said, it could get worse before it gets better... So like a decade, I think it's like, yeah, it doesn't seem like a decade. Feels like it's a decade.
predictions.prediction: San Francisco’s downtown office market will not return to a normal/healthy vacancy range (roughly 5–15%) for at least five years and possibly up to about a decade after 2023; i.e., sustained elevated vacancy will persist into at least the late 2020s and potentially early 2030s.

predictions.quote: I'm sticking by it. I think we're still going to have a recession
predictions.prediction: David Sacks maintains his prediction (as of April 28, 2023) that the U.S. economy will enter a recession in the near future, i.e., within the upcoming business cycle following this statement.

predictions.quote: the Merck exec was like, we're going to sell $1 billion of fetal bovine serum, and then we're going to sell zero because no one's going to be able to make money doing this
predictions.prediction: A Merck executive predicts that sales of fetal bovine serum used for cellular meat production will rise to approximately $1 billion in annual revenue and then rapidly fall to near zero because cellular-meat companies will not be able to make money at the required cost structure, causing that use case to collapse.

predictions.quote: it’s very likely that these companies may need several more years and several billion dollars. We are going to get there
predictions.prediction: Friedberg predicts that companies working on recombinant protein production and cellular meat will require several more years (on the order of a few years beyond 2023) and several additional billions of dollars of investment, but that they will ultimately succeed in making these technologies work at commercially viable, cost-competitive scales.

predictions.quote: eventually we'll get to that cost curve where they're ubiquitous for all proteins or for all types of cells
predictions.prediction: Over the long term, recombinant/synthetic-biology-based production methods will move far enough down the cost curve that they become ubiquitous for producing all major classes of proteins and cell types, displacing traditional animal-sourced production for those products.
